title: Cohort Orbit rollout calendar and exit criteria notebook (Nov 2026) - WIP
content:
Summary:
This is the working notebook for the 'Cohort Orbit' mini-rollout across three customer cohorts (alpha, beta, gamma). Purpose is to track the calendar, preflight checklists, measurable exit criteria, rollback scripts, telemetry postcards and quick release notes draft. This doc is intentionally terse — treat it as the operator clipboard during the 10-day stabilization window.

Scope and quick goals:
- Release scope: runtime change: dynamic-kv-cache v2 + small batching tweak (server-side). No model changes.
- Primary goals: 1) Validate latency SLOs at 99p for 512 tokens, 2) confirm no increase in token error-rate > 0.05% vs baseline, 3) measure unit cost delta (tokens/sec GPU) and keep within +8% budget.
- Secondary: confirm that Dedicated customers saw no config drift; Private deploys unaffected.

Owners and contacts:
- Release lead: Maya Rodriguez (pager: maya@redwood.ai, slack direct: @maya)
- SRE primary on-call: Ethan Park (pager)
- Serving runtime SME: Sofia Martinez
- Telemetry/observability: Noah Patel
- Rollback owner: Harper Liu
- Slack channel for launch: #release-cohort-orbit
- Pager rota: ENG-SRE on-call (ENG-SRE-rotation)

High-level rollout calendar (UTC):
- Day -7 (2026-11-01): Final preflight signoff, traffic simulation run, smoke PR verification.
- Day -3 (2026-11-05): Canary deploy to alpha cohort (1% traffic) during low window 03:00-06:00 UTC. Telemetry postcard baseline collected.
- Day 0 (2026-11-08): Gradual ramp to beta cohort (10% traffic) between 06:00-12:00 UTC if canary green.
- Day +1 (2026-11-09): Expand to gamma cohort (30% traffic) if beta stable OR hold and run additional load tests.
- Day +3 (2026-11-11): Full cohort rollout (100% targeted cohorts) and observe 48h stabilization window.
- Day +7 (2026-11-15): Post-release retro + decide permanent config promotion.

Runbook preflight checklist (must be green before Day -3):
- [ ] PRs merged: platform PRs tagged and merged (see linked PR #4682).
- [ ] Infra: kube manifests baked and validated in staging (kubeval, admission hooks).
- [ ] Canary image: image digest pinned in release manifest.
- [ ] DB migrations: none. If migration appears later, abort.
- [ ] Feature flags: dynamic-kv-cache.v2 behind rollout-flag. Ensure default OFF for non-cohort traffic.
- [ ] Capacity: reserved pool for Dedicated customers verified (alerts for GPU queue length > 60s).
- [ ] Observability: dashboards published and dashboard links posted to slack.
- [ ] Smoke tests: run smoke-suite v3.2 against canary and attach logs.
- [ ] Runbook posted: this doc linked in the release channel and pinned.

Exit criteria (quantitative; everything must pass to continue expansion):
1) Latency SLOs: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 400ms for 512-token requests within cohort traffic. Acceptable drift from baseline: p99 <= baseline_p99 + 25ms.
2) Error rates: 5xx + model-run errors combined <= baseline + 0.05% absolute.
3) Token cost delta: median tokens-per-second GPU must not be worse than +8% from staging baseline.
4) Prefix KV hit-rate: >= 85% for cached workloads where caching expected.
5) No negative customer-impact alerts from Dedicated tier (SEV >= 2).

Telemetry postcard plan (what to snapshot when):
- Canary snapshot (Day -3, 03:30 UTC): collect 15m window of traces, tok-per-sec, queue depth, schd latencies.
- Beta snapshot (Day 0, 07:00 UTC): collect 30m window and run difference-vs-baseline job.
- Gamma snapshot (Day +1, 10:00 UTC): collect 1h window, run SLA gating scripts.
- Stabilization windows: 5m sampling every 10m for first 12h, then 15m sampling for next 36h.
- SLI jobs: run nightly regression evals (eval suite: rolling-compat-v4) and post top-10 failing prompts to slack #release-cohort-orbit-failures.

Immediate rollback script (if any single exit criteria violates):
1) Announce in #release-cohort-orbit: "ROLLBACK: Cohort Orbit -> initiating rollback to prior manifest (digest: <prev-digest>)."
2) Trigger infrastructure roll (k8s rollout undo) for the affected cluster pool. Escalate to SRE on-call immediately after command.
3) Re-route cohort traffic to fallback model-variant (see routing policy: policy-id ORBIT-FALLBACK-3).
4) Start incident doc (template: INCIDENT-ROLLBACK) and keep rolling log in channel.
5) Postmortem owner assigned within 24h.

Smoke checks and quick commands (ops cheatsheet):
- smoke-run: ./tools/smoke.sh --endpoint https://canary.api.redwood.ai --suite smoke-v3
- check-latency: ./tools/check_sli.py --project orbit --window 15m --percentile 99
- re-route: ./tools/routing ctl set --policy ORBIT-FALLBACK-3 --cohort beta --percent 100
- gather-traces: ./tools/trace-collect --start -15m --end now --out /tmp/orbit-trace.json

Customer-facing release notes (draft):
Title: Cohort Orbit: backend KV cache and batching improvements (Nov 2026)
What changed: We rolled out an improved KV cache layer (dynamic-kv-cache v2) which reduces repeated prefix compute and adjusts batching heuristics to improve small-request tail latency. No customer-facing API changes.
Why it matters: Typical latency improvements for interactive requests; better tail behavior in heavy-multiplexed workloads. Some internal cost tradeoffs to optimize throughput.
Known limitations: Small number of special-case prefixes (legacy clients) may see lower cache hit-rate; mitigation in progress.
Support: If you observe increased latency or errors, please reach out to support@redwood.ai or file ENGOPS-2145.

Communications plan (short):
- T-minus 24h: post summary to #release-announce with expected windows and contact list.
- T-minus 1h: remind @oncall and product stakeholders with quick checklist.
- Post expand: publish short note to internal-status with immediate KPIs.
- Customer comms: for Dedicated customers only, send a synced email if any deviation > exit thresholds.

Outstanding risks & mitigations (notes to self):
- Risk: sudden regional GPU scheduling backlog during beta expand -> mitigation: bias new pods to spare pools and throttle ingress via token-bucket. Ticket: REL-400.
- Risk: telemetry regression job false positives due to timezone TTL mismatch -> mitigation: run half-hourly sync job and use UTC-only windows. Assigned: Noah.
- Question: Do we need an emergency feature-flag to force-disable batching for one cohort? If yes, create flag ORBIT-BATCH-BREAKER.

After-action retro template (fill after Day +7):
- What went well (3 bullets)
- What surprised us (3 bullets)
- Where did metrics diverge from expectations (list and attach charts)
- Action items (owner, ETA, priority)

Quick links (grab these when staging is green):
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4682
- Confluence plan: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/Cohort-Orbit-Plan
- Jira: ENGOPS-2145 (telemetry), REL-400 (capacity), PLAT-3301 (batching heuristics)

Notes to operators (loose):
- If you see token-cost spike but latency within SLO, pause expansion and run cost profiler; prefer to hold than to risk customer impact.
- Keep this notebook pinned in the channel; copy paste the rollback script header into the incident doc if triggered.

---
Last updated: 2026-11-08 by Maya (draft).
Unresolved: decision on ORBIT-BATCH-BREAKER flag (Sofia to confirm by Day -2).
